p.src: Now this day was Jia Jing’s birthday. Jia Zhen first packed sixteen large presentation boxes with the finest delicacies and some rare fruits, then ordered Jia Rong to lead the household servants and deliver them to Jia Jing. He told Jia Rong, “Watch carefully to see whether your great-grandfather is pleased. Once you have paid your respects, come back. Say to him, ‘My father, in obedience to your command, did not dare come. At home he led the entire household in bowing toward you and paying their respects.’” Having heard these instructions, Jia Rong immediately led the servants away.

p.src: Meanwhile, guests gradually began to arrive. Jia Lian and Jia Qiang arrived first. After inspecting the seating arrangements in the various rooms, they asked, “Is there any entertainment?” A servant replied, “Our master originally expected the old master to come home today, so he did not dare arrange any entertainment. When we heard the other day that the old master would not be coming after all, he ordered us to find a troupe of young actors and a shifan instrumental ensemble. They are now ready on the stage in the garden.”

p.src: Lady Xing, Lady Wang, Xifeng, and Baoyu arrived next, and Jia Zhen and Madam You welcomed them inside. Madam You’s mother was already there. After exchanging greetings, everyone courteously invited the others to be seated. Jia Zhen and Madam You personally served the tea and said, “The Old Lady is the matriarch of our clan, while my father is her nephew. On an occasion like this, we would not ordinarily presume to invite her. But the weather is pleasantly cool just now, and the chrysanthemums throughout the garden are in full bloom, so we hoped the Old Ancestress might come over to relieve her boredom and enjoy seeing all her children and grandchildren making merry. That was all we intended. Who would have thought that the Old Ancestress would decline to honor us with her presence?” Before Lady Wang could speak, Xifeng said, “Only yesterday the Old Lady was saying that she meant to come. But last night, when she saw Brother Bao and the others eating peaches, she developed a craving herself and ate more than half of one. Around the fifth watch she had to get up twice in succession, and this morning she felt rather weary. So she asked me to tell you, Cousin Zhen, that she absolutely could not come today. She also said that she wanted several of the best dishes, and that they must be cooked very soft.” Jia Zhen laughed. “I knew the Old Ancestress loved a lively gathering. If she was not coming today, there had to be some reason. Now that you explain it, I understand.”

p.src: Lady Wang said, “The other day I heard your elder sister say that Jia Rong’s wife was somewhat unwell. What exactly is the matter with her?” Madam You replied, “Her illness is a strange one. At the Mid-Autumn Festival last month, she stayed up half the night enjoying herself with the Old Lady and all you ladies, and she came home perfectly well. But after the twentieth she grew more listless with every passing day and lost all desire to eat. It has been more than half a month now. Her courses have not come for two months either.” Lady Xing interjected, “Could she be with child?” As they spoke, someone outside reported, “The Elder Master, the Second Master, and all the gentlemen of the family have arrived and are in the hall.” Jia Zhen hurried out. Only then did Madam You continue, “Some of the physicians we consulted before also said that she might be with child. But yesterday Feng Ziying recommended a former teacher of his who is highly skilled in medicine. After examining her, he said it was not pregnancy at all, but a very serious illness. He wrote a prescription yesterday. After one dose, her dizziness is a little better today, but there has been no marked improvement in anything else.” Xifeng said, “I knew that unless she was utterly unable to hold herself up, on a day like today she would certainly have forced herself to come.” Madam You said, “You saw her here on the third. She had already forced herself to stay up for half the day. It was only because she is so fond of you and your little girl that she lingered, reluctant to leave.” Xifeng’s eyes reddened for a long while. At last she said, “‘Storms may arise from a clear sky, and fortune or calamity may befall a person overnight’—how true that is! At her age, if anything should happen to her because of this illness, what pleasure would there be in life for the rest of us?” While they were still speaking, Jia Rong came in. After paying his respects to Lady Xing, Lady Wang, and Xifeng, he reported to Madam You, “Just now I went to deliver the food to my great-grandfather and told him that my father was at home attending upon the masters and entertaining all the gentlemen of the clan, and that in obedience to his command he had not dared come. My great-grandfather was very pleased and said, ‘That is as it should be.’ He told me to instruct Father and Mother to attend carefully upon the elder masters and ladies, and ordered me to look after my uncles, aunts, and elder cousins properly. He also said that the Treatise on Hidden Recompense must be engraved without delay, and ten thousand copies printed for distribution. I have already reported all of this to my father. Now I must hurry out and see that the elder masters and all the gentlemen of the family are served their meal.” Xifeng said, “Wait a moment, Rong. How exactly is your wife today?” Jia Rong frowned. “Bad! You will know when you go to see her later, Aunt.” Jia Rong then went out.

p.src: Madam You then asked Lady Xing and Lady Wang, “Would you ladies prefer to dine here, or shall we go and eat in the garden? The young actors are ready in the garden now.” Lady Wang said to Lady Xing, “We may as well finish our meal before going over. It will save a good deal of trouble.” “Very well,” said Lady Xing. Madam You thereupon instructed the married maids and older serving women, “Bring the meal quickly.” A chorus of assent came from outside, and each went off to fetch her assigned dishes. Before long, the meal was laid out. Madam You seated Lady Xing, Lady Wang, and her own mother in the places of honor, while she, Xifeng, and Baoyu took seats to the side. Lady Xing and Lady Wang said, “We came to offer birthday congratulations to the Elder Master, yet it seems as though we have come to celebrate our own birthdays instead!” Xifeng said, “The Elder Master has always loved peace and solitude. He has already perfected his spiritual discipline and may fairly be called an immortal. After what you ladies have just said, this is precisely what they mean by ‘the heart’s devotion is known to the gods.’” Her remark sent everyone in the room into laughter.

p.src: When Lady You's mother, Lady Xing, Lady Wang, and Xifeng had finished their meal, rinsed their mouths, and washed their hands, they were just saying that they would go into the garden when Jia Rong came in and said to Lady You, “The elder gentlemen and all the uncles, cousins, and brothers have finished eating too. The First Master said he had business at home, while the Second Master neither cares for opera nor likes noisy crowds, so they have both just left. All the other gentlemen of the family have been invited by Second Uncle Lian and Cousin Qiang to go and watch the opera. Just now, the princes of Nan'an, Dongping, Xining, and Beijing, as well as six noble houses including that of Niu, Duke of Zhenguo, and eight houses including that of Shi, Marquis of Zhongjing, all sent men with their visiting cards and birthday gifts. I reported everything to Father; the gifts have been placed in the accounts office for the time being, and all the gift lists have been entered in the register. The Master's cards acknowledging the gifts have been handed to the respective messengers, each messenger has received the customary gratuity, and all were given a meal before they left. Mother, you should invite the two ladies, Grandmother, and Aunt to go and sit in the garden.” Lady You replied, “We too have only just finished eating and were about to go over.”

p.src: Xifeng and Baoyu then accompanied Jia Rong to Qin-shi's quarters. After entering, they walked quietly to the doorway of the inner room. Qin-shi made to rise when she saw them, but Xifeng said, “Do not get up so quickly—you may grow dizzy.” Xifeng hurried forward two steps, took Qin-shi by the hand, and exclaimed, “My dear! How have you grown so thin in only a few days since I last saw you!” She then sat down on the padded mat where Qin-shi was sitting. Baoyu also asked after her health and seated himself on a chair opposite. Jia Rong called out, “Bring tea quickly! Aunt and Second Uncle had none in the main room.”

p.src: Holding Xifeng's hand, Qin-shi forced a smile and said, “All this is because I was born without good fortune. I married into such a family, and my parents-in-law treat me as though I were their own daughter. Your nephew may be young, Aunt, but he respects me and I respect him; we have never once exchanged an angry word. Among all the elders and younger members of the family—not to mention you, Aunt—there is no one who has not cherished me or been kind to me. But now that I have fallen ill, not a trace of my proud spirit remains. I have not been able to serve my parents-in-law dutifully for even a single day; and though you cherish me so, Aunt, even if I had ten parts of filial devotion in my heart, I can no longer put any of it into practice. I cannot help thinking that I may not live to see the New Year.”

p.src: Baoyu was gazing at the painting Spring Slumber of the Begonia and the couplet written by Qin Taixu—“Tender chill locks dreams because the spring is cold; sweet fragrance enfolds one, for it is the scent of wine”—when he involuntarily recalled the afternoon nap he had taken here and his dream of the Land of Illusion. He was lost in thought when he heard Qin-shi's words. They pierced his heart like a myriad arrows, and tears began to stream down his face before he knew it. Though Xifeng was deeply grieved herself, she feared that if the invalid saw them all like this, it would only add to her sorrow and defeat the purpose of their visit to comfort and encourage her. Seeing Baoyu in this state, she said, “Brother Bao, you are far too sentimental. She is ill and merely speaking despondently—how could things possibly have come to such a pass already? Besides, she is still so young. If every slight illness makes her imagine this and that, is she not merely making herself even sicker?” Jia Rong said, “Her illness needs no special remedy. So long as she can take some food, there will be nothing to fear.” Xifeng said, “Brother Bao, your mother is calling for you to come quickly. Do not keep on like this here, or you will upset your niece-in-law as well. Your mother will be worrying about you too.” She then said to Jia Rong, “You go on ahead with your Uncle Bao. I shall sit here a little longer.” At this, Jia Rong accompanied Baoyu to the Garden of Congregated Fragrance.

p.src: Xifeng stayed behind and comforted Qin-shi further, speaking softly to her at length from the heart. Only after Lady You had sent for her two or three times did Xifeng say to Qin-shi, “Take good care of yourself. I shall come and see you again. It must be Heaven's will that you recover, for only the other day someone recommended this excellent physician. There is no longer anything to fear.” Qin-shi smiled and said, “Even if he were an immortal, he might cure an illness but could not alter fate. Aunt, I know that with this illness I am merely living out my remaining days.” Xifeng said, “If you persist in thinking that way, how can you ever recover? You must set your mind at ease. Besides, I heard the physician say that if it went untreated, the danger would be that you might not fare well in the spring. It is only the middle of the ninth month now, so there are still four or five months ahead. What illness could not be cured in that time? If ours were a family unable to afford ginseng, the outcome might be uncertain. But if your parents-in-law hear that it can cure you, they could afford not merely two qian of ginseng a day, but even two jin. Take good care of yourself. I am going to the garden now.” Qin-shi added, “Forgive me, Aunt, for being unable to accompany you. When you have leisure, please come and see me often. We women can sit together and talk a while.” At these words, Xifeng's eyes reddened once more despite herself, and she said, “Whenever I have time, I shall be sure to come and see you.” Xifeng then led the elderly attendants and maids who had accompanied her, together with the married servants and matrons of the Ning Mansion, around through an inner side gate into the garden. There she beheld:

p.src: Yellow flowers carpeted the ground, while white willows stretched across the slope. A little bridge led to a stream like that of Ruoye, and a winding path joined the road to Tiantai. Clear water rushed among the rocks; fragrance drifted from the hedges; red leaves fluttered on the treetops, and the sparse woods were picturesque. The west wind had suddenly freshened, silencing the last orioles; the warm sun shone mildly, and crickets added their voices. Looking southeast, one saw several pavilions built against the hills; gazing northwest, three chambers stood beside the water. The music of reed pipes filled the ear, awakening a distinctive, secluded charm. Silken-clad figures passed through the grove, adding still more grace to the scene.

p.src: Xifeng was admiring the garden scenery, praising it as she walked slowly onward. Suddenly a man emerged from behind an artificial rock, came forward, and greeted her: “My respects, cousin.” Startled by his sudden appearance, Xifeng drew back and said, “Why, isn’t this Cousin Rui?” Jia Rui said, “Can it be that even you no longer recognize me, cousin? Who else could it be but me!” “It isn’t that I failed to recognize you,” replied Xifeng. “You appeared so suddenly that I never imagined you would be here.” Jia Rui said, “It must be fate that has brought you and me together, cousin. I slipped away from the banquet just now to stroll for a while in this quiet place, never expecting to meet you coming this way too. Is that not fate?” As he spoke, he kept casting sidelong glances at Xifeng.

p.src: Xifeng was clever; seeing his manner, how could she fail to guess most of what was in his mind? Feigning a smile, she said to Jia Rui, “No wonder your cousin often mentions you and says how admirable you are. Now that I have met you and heard these few words, I can tell that you are intelligent and good-natured. I must go to the ladies now, so I cannot stay and talk; when we are both at leisure, we shall speak again.” Jia Rui said, “I have wanted to call at your home and pay my respects, cousin, but I feared that, being young, you might not readily receive visitors.” Xifeng gave another feigned smile. “We are all one family and kin. What need is there to speak of being young or not?” Hearing this, Jia Rui could scarcely believe he had met with such extraordinary good fortune that day, and his expression became even more indecent and unsightly. Xifeng said, “You had better return to the feast quickly, or they may catch you and make you drink a forfeit.” At these words, half Jia Rui’s body went numb. He walked slowly away, repeatedly turning his head to look back. Xifeng deliberately slowed her steps. When she saw that he had gone some distance, she thought to herself, “So this is what they mean by knowing a man’s face but not his heart! How can there be such a beast? If he persists in this, I shall find a way to make him die at my hands; then he will learn what I am capable of!” Only then did Xifeng continue on her way. As she rounded another hillside, she saw two or three elderly serving women hurrying toward her. When they saw Xifeng, they smiled and said, “Our mistress was beside herself because you still had not come, Second Mistress, and sent us servants to invite you again.” Xifeng said, “Your mistress is always as impatient as a hurrying ghost.” Walking at an unhurried pace, Xifeng asked, “How many pieces have they performed?” One of the women replied, “Eight or nine.” While they were speaking, they reached the rear entrance of Tianxiang Tower, where Baoyu was playing with a group of maids. Xifeng said, “Brother Bao, do not be too mischievous.” A maid said, “The ladies are all seated upstairs. Please go up this way, Mistress.”

u.src: Xifeng was clever; seeing his manner, how could she fail to guess most of what was in his mind? Feigning a smile, she said to Jia Rui, “No wonder your cousin often mentions you and says how admirable you are.
Now that I have met you and heard these few words, I can tell that you are intelligent and good-natured.
I must go to the ladies now, so I cannot stay and talk; when we are both at leisure, we shall speak again.”
Jia Rui said, “I have wanted to call at your home and pay my respects, cousin, but I feared that, being young, you might not readily receive visitors.”
Xifeng gave another feigned smile. “We are all one family and kin. What need is there to speak of being young or not?”
Hearing this, Jia Rui could scarcely believe he had met with such extraordinary good fortune that day, and his expression became even more indecent and unsightly.
Xifeng said, “You had better return to the feast quickly, or they may catch you and make you drink a forfeit.”
At these words, half Jia Rui’s body went numb. He walked slowly away, repeatedly turning his head to look back.

Xifeng deliberately slowed her steps. When she saw that he had gone some distance, she thought to herself, “So this is what they mean by knowing a man’s face but not his heart! How can there be such a beast?
If he persists in this, I shall find a way to make him die at my hands; then he will learn what I am capable of!”
Only then did Xifeng continue on her way.

As she rounded another hillside, she saw two or three elderly serving women hurrying toward her. When they saw Xifeng, they smiled and said, “Our mistress was beside herself because you still had not come, Second Mistress, and sent us servants to invite you again.”
Xifeng said, “Your mistress is always as impatient as a hurrying ghost.”
Walking at an unhurried pace, Xifeng asked, “How many pieces have they performed?”
One of the women replied, “Eight or nine.”
While they were speaking, they reached the rear entrance of Tianxiang Tower, where Baoyu was playing with a group of maids.
Xifeng said, “Brother Bao, do not be too mischievous.”
A maid said, “The ladies are all seated upstairs. Please go up this way, Mistress.”

p.src: Hearing this, Xifeng gathered up her gown and ascended at a measured pace, to find Madam You already waiting at the head of the stairs. Madam You said with a smile, “You and your little niece are so fond of each other that whenever you meet, you cannot bear to come away. You might as well move in and live with her tomorrow. Sit down, and let me first offer you a cup.” Xifeng thereupon asked permission to sit before Madams Xing and Wang, exchanged the proper courtesies with Madam You’s mother, and then sat at Madam You’s table once more to drink wine and watch the opera. Madam You ordered the programme brought and asked Xifeng to choose a piece. Xifeng said, “With our honored relative and the ladies present, how could I presume to choose?” Madams Xing and Wang said, “Our honored relative and we have already chosen several. Pick two good pieces for us to enjoy.” Xifeng rose and assented, then took the programme and read it from the beginning. She chose The Return of the Soul and Ballad Recitation, handed the programme back, and said, “When the present performance of The Two Patents of Nobility is over, they can sing these two; by then it will be about time to leave.” Madam Wang said, “Exactly. We ought to let your elder cousin and his wife rest early too; with all their responsibilities, their minds cannot be at ease.” Madam You said, “You ladies so seldom visit; it is more enjoyable if we all sit together a little longer. The hour is still early.” Xifeng stood and looked down from the tower. “Where have all the gentlemen gone?” she asked. An elderly serving woman beside her said, “The gentlemen have just gone to Ningxi Pavilion. They took the shifan musicians there and are drinking.” Xifeng said, “They find it too constrained here, but who knows what they are up to behind our backs!” Madam You laughed. “Not everyone is as proper as you are.” Thus they talked and laughed until all the chosen pieces had been performed; only then was the wine feast cleared and the meal served. After eating, they all left the garden and sat in the main apartments. Once they had taken tea, they ordered their carriages prepared and bade farewell to Madam You’s mother. Madam You came out to see them off with the concubines and the household’s elderly and married women servants. Jia Zhen and the younger men of the clan stood waiting beside the carriages. On seeing Madams Xing and Wang, he said, “Please come again tomorrow for another visit, aunts.” Madam Wang replied, “No, no. We have sat here the whole day and are tired. We shall rest tomorrow.” They then all boarded their carriages and departed. Jia Rui still cast frequent sidelong glances at Xifeng. After Jia Zhen and the others had gone inside, Li Gui brought Baoyu’s horse over. Baoyu mounted and followed Madam Wang home. Jia Zhen and the other brothers and nephews of the clan then ate their evening meal, after which everyone dispersed.

p.src: The next day, the clansmen and their families made merry for another full day, but there is no need to recount it in detail. After that, Xifeng often came in person to see Lady Qin. On some days Lady Qin seemed a little better; on others she remained as she had been. Jia Zhen, Lady You, and Jia Rong were desperately worried.

p.src: Now Jia Rui came to Rong Mansion several times, but on every occasion he happened to find that Xifeng had gone over to Ning Mansion. That year the Winter Solstice fell on the thirtieth day of the eleventh month. During the days around the festival, Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and Xifeng sent someone every day to inquire after Lady Qin, and those who returned all reported, “These past few days she has shown no sign of worsening, but neither has she improved much.” Lady Wang said to Grandmother Jia, “With an illness like this, if she can pass such a major festival without getting worse, there is considerable hope for her.” “Indeed,” said Grandmother Jia. “Such a fine child! If anything should happen to her, it would break our hearts.” As she spoke, sorrow welled up in her heart, and she said to Xifeng, “You two have always been very close. Tomorrow is the first day of the month; once tomorrow is past, go and see her again the day after. Observe her condition carefully. If she is a little better, come back and tell me, so that I too may have something to gladden me. And have the foods she usually enjoys prepared from time to time and sent over to her.” Xifeng promised to do each and every thing.

p.src: On the second day, after breakfast, Xifeng went to Ning Mansion. When she saw Lady Qin, she found that although the illness had not grown much worse, all the flesh had wasted from her face and body. She sat with Lady Qin for a long while, chatting about ordinary matters, and once again comforted her by saying that the illness was nothing to fear. Lady Qin said, “Whether I shall recover or not will be known by spring. Now that the Winter Solstice has passed without anything happening, perhaps I may yet recover. Aunt, please tell the Old Lady and Lady Wang not to worry. Yesterday I even ate two pieces of the date-paste yam cake the Old Lady sent me, and they seemed to digest quite well.” “I shall have some more sent to you tomorrow,” said Xifeng. I will go and see your mother-in-law, and then I must hurry back to report to the Old Lady.” Lady Qin said, “Aunt, please give my respects to the Old Lady and Lady Wang.”

p.src: Xifeng assented and came out, then went to Lady You’s principal room and sat down. Lady You asked, “Tell me candidly: how does my daughter-in-law look to you?” Xifeng lowered her head for a long while before saying, “There is truly nothing more to be done. You ought to begin arranging all the things needed for her funeral. Perhaps making such preparations may even ward the event off.” Lady You said, “I too have had people make preparations in secret. It is only that we cannot obtain good timber for that particular article, so for the time being we must proceed with it slowly.” Xifeng drank some tea and talked for a while, then said, “I must hurry back and report to the Old Lady.” Lady You said, “Break it to her gently; do not frighten the Old Lady.” “I know,” replied Xifeng. Xifeng then returned home. When she arrived and saw Grandmother Jia, she said, “Rong’s wife sends her respects to you, Old Lady, and bows before you. She says she is somewhat better and begs her venerable ancestress not to worry. As soon as she is a little better still, she intends to come and bow to her venerable ancestress in person.” Grandmother Jia asked, “How did she appear to you?” “For the present there is no cause for alarm,” said Xifeng. “Her spirits are still quite good.” On hearing this, Grandmother Jia pondered for a long while, then said to Xifeng, “Go and change your clothes and rest.”

p.src: Xifeng assented and withdrew. After paying her respects to Lady Wang, she returned to her own quarters, where Ping’er helped her change into everyday clothes that had been warmed for her. As soon as Xifeng sat down, she asked, “Has anything happened at home?” Ping’er brought over a cup of tea and handed it to her, saying, “Nothing has happened. Wang’er’s wife brought in the interest on those three hundred taels of silver, and I received it. Also, Master Rui sent someone to ask whether you were at home. He wishes to come and pay his respects and speak with you.” Xifeng gave a contemptuous snort. “The brute is bent on courting death. Let us see what happens when he comes!” Ping’er asked, “Why does Master Rui keep coming here?” Xifeng then told Ping’er all about meeting him in the garden of Ning Mansion in the ninth month and everything he had said. Ping’er said, “A mangy toad craving swan’s flesh! That shameless, depraved scoundrel—may he die a miserable death for entertaining such a thought!” Xifeng said, “When he comes, I shall know how to deal with him.” What will happen when Jia Rui comes remains unknown; listen to the next chapter for the explanation.
